claims.text: Active learning with uncertainty quantification can guide sparse, targeted ab initio molecular-dynamics corrections when training machine-learned interatomic potentials.
This framework will substantially reduce the computational cost of fusion and high-temperature free-energy calculations.
The framework will faithfully capture vibrational entropy.
The framework will faithfully capture anharmonic effects.
The framework will faithfully capture electron–vibration coupling effects.
High-quality ab initio data for both solid and liquid phases exist for Al, Cu, and Al–Cu systems.
Strategically selected ab initio MD snapshots near melting can be used to train the proposed interatomic potential.
Uncertainty estimates can identify regions requiring additional ab initio data and thereby adaptively refine the potential.
The method will be evaluated for both solid and liquid phases over approximately 0.9–1.1 Tm.
A sparsely corrected ML potential-energy surface can accurately reconstruct the full free-energy landscape.
Limiting ab initio MD snapshots to configurations selected by active-learning uncertainty metrics reduces the number of costly first-principles calculations.
Iterative ML-potential refinement can retain the essential contributions needed for accurate free energies.
The proposed method will reduce computational cost by roughly one order of magnitude relative to explicit ab initio MD workflows.
Predicted fusion free energies and derived thermodynamic observables will be competitive with or more accurate than TOR-TILD in the targeted temperature range.
Initial applicability is restricted to elemental and binary systems near melting, while application to multicomponent high-entropy alloys requires further validation.
Generalization to multicomponent high-entropy systems and broader temperature ranges is uncertain.
Prior evidence supports the feasibility of active-learning ML potentials for free-energy calculations.
